To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a new method for learning similarity metrics in a data-driven fashion, which is based on learned feature representations, and we show that our method is superior to VAEs with pixel-wise similarity measures in the reconstruction of images.

(1) we present an autoencoder architecture that learns a similarity measure based on a learned feature representation and (2) that we demonstrate that this similarity measure is better suited for image generation than a simple Euclidean distance in data space.

we present a method to improve the performance of autoencoders in terms of visual quality, that it learns an embedding in the latent space that allows for simple modification of high-level visual features and that it can be applied to a variety of data modalities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving generative models by using learned similarity measures in the latent space.
the problem of learning a data distribution that is invariant to certain transformations, e.g. translations.
how to use learned representations to better capture data distributions and how to exploit these representations to manipulate data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our method is a powerful tool to generate images that are visually plausible, while also allowing for a high degree of control in terms of high level visual features, which is a desirable property in many applications.
the proposed model can learn a better representation of the input data, which is more robust against transformations and more similar to the original input data.
we show how to learn a similarity measure in a way that allows to modify abstract visual features.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a new method that can generate realistic images and that can learn to modify high-level features of the images in an arithmetic manner.
we show how to learn a similarity metric for a specific data distribution and how this metric can be used to improve the quality of the reconstruction.
we present an autoencoder architecture that learns to measure the similarity in the data space and can be used for image generation and manipulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
learned similarity measures offer a new perspective on the autoencoding problem, which we hope will inspire further work in this direction.
we can use learned representations to better capture data similarities and thereby improve autoencoding.
learned similarity metrics can help to improve the quality of generative models.
